title: Atmospheric river-driven delivery of Patagonian bioaerosol to the Antarctic Peninsula
description: Airborne, soil, rhizosphere, sediment and seawater microbial communities sampled along a 1,500 km transect from southern Patagonia (Punta Arenas, San Gregorio, Porvenir, Puerto Natales, Puerto Williams; Chile) to the Antarctic Peninsula (Risopatron Base, Robert Island; Yelcho Base, Doumer Island) in the austral summer of 2021 2022, with daily air sampling at Risopatron bracketing the 7-8 February 2022 atmospheric river. Air was collected with a Coriolis micro wet-cyclone sampler (54 m3 per sample). Data comprise 16S rRNA gene (V4), ITS1 and 18S rRNA gene amplicons for 198 samples including negative controls (Coriolis, deposition and buffer controls) and seawater, sediment samples from Union Glacier collected in November 2021, and 15 shotgun metagenomes of MDA-amplified air DNA (Puerto Williams and Risopatron).
